method_card.title: My Town and Local Area
method_card.content:
This lesson covers places in your town or village and how to describe what you can do there. You will use hay for existence and se puede + infinitive for general statements about what can be done.

SpanishEnglish
la ciudadthe city
el pueblothe village / small town
el barriothe neighbourhood
el centro de la ciudadthe town centre
el parquethe park
el mercadothe market
la bibliotecathe library
el ayuntamientothe town hall
la piscinathe swimming pool
el polideportivothe sports centre
haythere is / there are
se puede + infinitiveyou can / one can
lo mejor es quethe best thing is that
lo peor es quethe worst thing is that

Grammar focus — Hay vs Estar: Use hay for existence: Hay una piscina en mi barrio (There is a swimming pool in my neighbourhood). Use está / están for the location of a specific, known item: La piscina está cerca del parque (The swimming pool is near the park). NEVER use hay with a definite article: say hay una piscina, never hay la piscina.

Se puede + infinitive is the impersonal way to say what can be done in a place: Se puede nadar (you can swim), Se puede ir de compras (you can go shopping). The negative is No se puede hacer mucho (You can't do much).

Model paragraph: Vivo en un pueblo pequeño. Hay un parque, una biblioteca y muchas tiendas. Lo mejor es que es tranquilo, pero lo peor es que no hay cine. Mi ciudad ideal tendría un polideportivo y más restaurantes. (I live in a small village. There is a park, a library, and many shops. The best thing is that it is quiet, but the worst thing is that there is no cinema. My ideal city would have a sports centre and more restaurants.)
steps: Learn the key vocabulary for places in town and local area
Master hay for existence and estar for location of a specific place
Use se puede + infinitive to say what you can do in your area
Give balanced opinions using lo mejor es que and lo peor es que
Build sentences about your ideal city using the conditional tendría / habría

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — town descriptions appear across all papers each year

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'En mi barrio hay un parque y se puede ir de compras.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: En mi barrio = In my neighbourhood. Hay = there is / there are.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Un parque = a park. Se puede = you can / one can. Ir de compras = go shopping.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: In my neighbourhood there is a park and you can go shopping.

worked_examples.question: Which is correct: 'Hay el mercado en el centro' or 'Hay un mercado en el centro'?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Hay expresses existence. It is NEVER followed by a definite article (el, la, los, las).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Hay el mercado is wrong. Use the indefinite article: hay un mercado.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Hay un mercado en el centro. (There is a market in the town centre.) The definite article is used with está for location: El mercado está en el centro.

worked_examples.question: How do you express 'My ideal city would have a sports centre and there would be less traffic' in Spanish?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: 'Would have' in Spanish uses the conditional: tener → tendría (it would have).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: 'There would be' = habría (conditional of hay). Menos tráfico = less traffic.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Mi ciudad ideal tendría un polideportivo y habría menos tráfico.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish places in town to their English meaning
Match the Spanish places to their English meaning
Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: ir de compras en el centro.

gaps.correct_explain: hay means 'there is' or 'there are'. It is used to express existence.

wrong.es: es means 'is'. To say something exists in a place, use hay.
wrong.está: está means 'is located'. Use hay (not está) to say there is a park in general.

gaps.rule: Se puede + infinitive = you can / one can
gaps.correct_explain: se puede is the impersonal form meaning 'you can' or 'one can', followed by an infinitive.

wrong.puedo: puedo means 'I can'. Se puede is the impersonal 'you can' used for general statements about a place.

gaps.rule: Opinion phrase: lo mejor es que
gaps.correct_explain: Lo mejor es que means 'The best thing is that'.

wrong.bueno: bueno means 'good'. The set phrase for 'the best thing' is lo mejor.

gaps.rule: Opinion phrase: lo peor es que
gaps.correct_explain: Lo peor es que means 'The worst thing is that'.

wrong.malo: malo means 'bad'. The set phrase for 'the worst thing' is lo peor.

bronze.question: What does 'No hay nada que hacer en mi pueblo' mean?
options: There is nothing to do in my village
There is a lot to do in my village

bronze.question: What does 'Mi ciudad ideal tendría un cine y muchos restaurantes' mean?
options: My ideal city would have a cinema and many restaurants
My city has a cinema and many restaurants
My city had a cinema and many restaurants
I want a city with a cinema and restaurants

bronze.source_text: Me gusta vivir aquí porque es tranquilo, pero no hay cine.
model_answers: I like living here because it is quiet, but there is no cinema.
hints: me gusta vivir = I like living

bronze.question: Listen and type what you hear
bronze.audio_text: Vivo en un pueblo pequeño pero bonito.
bronze.correct_text: Vivo en un pueblo pequeño pero bonito.
bronze.translation: I live in a small but pretty village.

silver.question: Complete the sentence
silver.english: My village is **quieter** than the city but there **isn't** much for young people.

gaps.correct_explain: tranquilo = quiet. Más tranquilo que = quieter than. Pueblo is masculine, so no -a ending.

wrong.ruidoso: ruidoso means 'noisy' — the opposite of what the sentence needs.

gaps.correct_explain: no hay = there isn't / there aren't. Hay is used for existence.

wrong.está: está refers to location of a specific thing. We need 'there isn't' = no hay.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Hay demasiado tráfico y demasiado contaminación en la ciudad.
silver.explanation: The second demasiado modifies contaminación, which is feminine. It must agree: demasiada contaminación. The first demasiado is correct because tráfico is masculine.
silver.translation: There is too much traffic and too much pollution in the city.

silver.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
silver.english: You can go shopping and swim in the pool.

distractor_labels.puedo: wrong form — puedo means 'I can'. The impersonal 'you can' in a place context is se puede

silver.source_text: I like living here because it is quiet. The best thing is that there is a park.
model_answers: Me gusta vivir aquí porque es tranquilo. Lo mejor es que hay un parque.
hints: I like living = me gusta vivir

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

gold.source_text: I live in a small village. The best thing is that it is quiet. The worst thing is that there is nothing to do for young people. My ideal city would have a cinema, a sports centre, and less traffic.
model_answers: Vivo en un pueblo pequeño. Lo mejor es que es tranquilo. Lo peor es que no hay nada que hacer para los jóvenes. Mi ciudad ideal tendría un cine, un polideportivo y menos tráfico.

Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
gold.english: There would be less traffic and more green spaces in my ideal city.

distractor_labels.Hay: wrong tense — Hay is present (there is). 'There would be' is conditional: Habría
distractor_labels.mucho: wrong word — the sentence says 'more' (más), not 'a lot of' (mucho)
distractor_labels.verde: wrong number — espacios is plural, so the adjective must also be plural: verdes

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are meeting a Spanish friend in town and they ask you about where you live and what there is to do.

bullets.prompt: Describe your town — say what there is and what you can do.
bullets.model_answer: Vivo en un pueblo pequeño. Hay un parque, muchas tiendas y un polideportivo. Se puede ir de compras y nadar en la piscina.
bullets.note: hay + se puede + infinitive — use impersonal se puede for what is possible in the town

bullets.prompt: Give your opinion — say the best and worst things about your town.
bullets.model_answer: Lo mejor es que es tranquilo y hay mucho que hacer. Lo peor es que no hay cine y el transporte público es malo.
bullets.note: lo mejor / lo peor opinion phrases — very common in the writing and speaking exams

bullets.prompt: Compare your town with a nearby city.
bullets.model_answer: La ciudad es más ruidosa pero tiene más tiendas y restaurantes. Mi pueblo es más tranquilo que la ciudad.
bullets.note: comparatives: más + adjective + que; check adjective agreement (ruidosa agrees with ciudad, feminine)

bullets.model_answer: Mi ciudad ideal tendría un cine, muchos restaurantes y habría menos tráfico y más zonas verdes.
bullets.note: conditional tendría / habría for ideal city — useful for the extended writing task

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Mi ciudad ideal tendría un cine, una piscina y muchos restaurantes, y habría menos tráfico y más espacios verdes.
gold.correct_text: Mi ciudad ideal tendría un cine, una piscina y muchos restaurantes, y habría menos tráfico y más espacios verdes.
gold.translation: My ideal city would have a cinema, a pool, and many restaurants, and there would be less traffic and more green spaces.

gold.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
gold.sentence: Si viviera en la ciudad, podría ir al cine y se puede hacer más cosas.
gold.explanation: In a hypothetical si clause with the subjunctive (viviera), the result clause needs the conditional: se podrían hacer (one would be able to do), not se puede (one can — present tense).
gold.translation: If I lived in the city, I could go to the cinema and one would be able to do more things.
